title: Dilucidationes super methodo elegantissima, qua illustris de la Grange usus est in integranda aequatione differentiali dx/√X = dy/√Y

deep.reconstruction:
Context: Euler is rederiving Lagrange's integration of dx/sqrt(X) = dy/sqrt(Y), where X = A + Bx + Cx^2 + Dx^3 + Ex^4 and Y is the same polynomial in y. Lagrange's method gives an integral that can be written Delta(x-y)^2 - V = ±2 sqrt(XY), with V = 2A + B(x+y) + 2Cxy + Dxy(x+y) + 2Ex^2y^2 and Delta (= Gamma) the arbitrary constant. Squaring gives (Delta(x-y)^2 - V)^2 = 4XY. Pages 39-40 show that 4XY - V^2 contains the factor (x-y)^2. After dividing it out, the rationalized integral is Gamma^2(x-y)^2 - 2Gamma V = (4XY - V^2)/(x-y)^2.

§44 moves everything to one side and uses (x±y)^2 = (x^2+y^2) ± 2xy. Comparing coefficients with Euler's own 'canonical' symmetric biquadratic, alpha + 2beta(x+y) + gamma(x^2+y^2) + 2delta xy + 2epsilon xy(x+y) + zeta x^2y^2 = 0 (from his 1750s work on elliptic addition), gives:
- alpha = 4AC + 4Gamma A - B^2
- beta = 2AD + Gamma B
- gamma = 4AE - Gamma^2
- delta = BD + 4AE + Gamma^2 + 2Gamma C
- epsilon = 2BE + Gamma D
- zeta = 4CE + 4Gamma E - D^2

This is an explicit dictionary between Lagrange's integral and Euler's canonical addition relation, with the free constant Gamma.

§45 remarks that the rationalized (squared) relation is the product of the two factors Delta(x-y)^2 - V ± 2 sqrt(XY). It therefore integrates both dx/sqrt X - dy/sqrt Y = 0 and dx/sqrt X + dy/sqrt Y = 0, one factor each.

§46 recalls an earlier (§8) alternative form of the integral: (M sqrt Y + N sqrt X)/(x-y)^3 = const, with explicit symmetric polynomials M and N. On the next page Euler admits he cannot easily see directly how this form agrees with the Lagrange form, though he is sure it does.
errors: No errors on this page. I verified all six coefficients alpha..zeta by expanding §43: e.g. the xy coefficient is 8AE + 2BD + 2Gamma^2 + 4Gamma C = 2delta. I also checked M and N in special cases: for X = A + Bx with u = sqrt X, v = sqrt Y, one gets M v + N u = (u+v)^3 and x - y = (u^2 - v^2)/B, so the ratio is B^3/(u-v)^3, constant exactly when sqrt X - sqrt Y is constant.
Previous page (§43): the term printed/transcribed as '+2Gamma C(x+y)' must be '+2Gamma B(x+y)'. This is consistent with beta = 2AD + Gamma B here; check the scan of p.39.
Next page: 'M-N ... +4Exy(x+y(x-y)' is missing a parenthesis; it should read 4Exy(x+y)(x-y).

ideas.what: Explicit identification of Lagrange's algebraic integral of the Euler equation with Euler's canonical symmetric biquadratic, coefficients given as functions of A..E and the free constant Gamma
ideas.modern_name: Symmetric biquadratic (Euler) addition relation / correspondence for the elliptic addition law
ideas.where_published: E506 itself (Acta Acad. Sci. Petrop. 1778:I, publ. 1781; Opera omnia I.21); canonical form in E251 and related papers

ideas.what: The rationalized integral covers both dx/sqrtX = dy/sqrtY and dx/sqrtX = -dy/sqrtY, being the product of two conjugate factors
ideas.modern_name: Rationalization / norm of an algebraic integral; both branches of the addition correspondence
ideas.where_published: Earlier Euler papers on elliptic integrals (e.g. Institutiones calculi integralis I) and E506

ideas.what: Alternative integral (M sqrtY + N sqrtX)/(x-y)^3 = const with explicit symmetric polynomials M, N
ideas.modern_name: Algebraic first integral of the Euler differential equation (alternative normalization of the constant)

missed.claim: Euler says he does not see directly how the cubic-denominator form (M sqrtY + N sqrtX)/(x-y)^3 = C agrees with Lagrange's form, though he is certain it does. A direct algebraic reconciliation would express C as an explicit function of Delta. It is a minor thread, likely resolvable by routine algebra, and probably treated implicitly in later textbooks.
missed.quote: Interim tamen haud facile intelligitur, quomodo haec forma cum ante inuenta conſentiat
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Minor. Only of pedagogical or historical interest; the equivalence follows from uniqueness of the algebraic integral up to a function of the constant.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a routine, correct coefficient matching between Lagrange's integral and Euler's well-known canonical symmetric biquadratic. It also notes the familiar fact that the squared relation covers both sign cases. All of this is in the published E506 and well-known context.
transcription_corrections: Transcription of this page matches the image; Gamma^2 and Gamma Gamma are used interchangeably in the original.
Previous page §43: '+2ΓC(x+y)' should be '+2ΓB(x+y)', either a print misprint or a transcription error.
